_comment: Cached on-device classifier used when the AI sidecar is unreachable or the demo-mode toggle is on. Algorithm: lowercase SMS body, then (1) substring-match against examples, (2) sweep scam_keywords, (3) sweep safe_keywords, (4) fall back to default_unverifiable.

examples.reasoning: Unsolicited prize-win claim is a classic scam pattern.
Family-impersonation 'Hi Mum' scam from an unknown number requesting urgent money.
Family-impersonation 'Hi Mom' scam from an unknown number requesting urgent money.
Phone-back fraud impersonating a bank's fraud team.
Suspicious typosquat of the Linkt brand.
Suspicious typosquat of the Australia Post brand.
ATO-impersonation refund phishing — the ATO never sends refunds via SMS link.
myGov-impersonation phishing — 'my-gov.au-secure.com' is not a gov.au domain, and myGov never asks you to reactivate your account through an SMS link.
Subscription-billing phishing impersonating Netflix; the lookalike domain harvests card details rather than netflix.com.
Cleartext HTTP link in an SMS is a phishing red flag.
Standard OTP message with no link or call to action.
